title: OpenApe Pods: interactive UI development with Vite
goal: Develop the actual Pods frontend with Vite and test data, then use the same UI with Electron and the existing backend by selecting the appropriate adapter and running the normal build.
summary: Separate the frontend from its data transport for Automations, Decisions and Pod details. Demo, Electron and the browser/backend use the same components and UI behavior through typed adapters; realistic scenarios make iteration fast, while contract and browser tests keep the real integrations working.

problem.statement: The UI mixes shared components with direct Electron access and separate local/remote orchestration.
problem.impact: A demo alone could evolve separately and leave repeated integration work for every UI change.
problem.approach: Use a shared frontend with injected adapters, and complete and test the real adapters as part of this change.
problem.outcome: UI edits made in Vite reach Electron and the backend-connected browser through the normal build without copying components or rewriting data access.

context: Implemented from canonical main 49fef2b3a8d5b1d91c7df56735a44e266c25b489 in the isolated feature/issue-1478-pods-ui-dev worktree. Existing PodAccess and remotePodAccess remain the editor boundary; the workspace controller is now shared and native access is injected. The current domain commands and scrolling Pod page were reused. Actual local checks and inspected screenshots are linked below; this record does not claim deployment or signed installation.
scope: Automations: existing map/list switch, grouping and filters, selection, detail panel, pause/resume and simulated run.
Decisions: realistic routing questions, single and group choices, counters and resolved state; demonstrate a rejected action and a successful retry.
Pod details: overview, script and permissions inspection, public variables, settings and run history with logs; edit description, one public variable and schedule through existing controls.
A small demo toolbar offers scenario selection, reset and visible simulation status. German is the initial UI language.
Use existing scripts and browser-test infrastructure; add only dev:ui as a new package command. Document startup, scenarios and supported actions.

Complete the shared frontend boundary and wire demo, Electron and existing backend adapters for the agreed three areas within this feature. Moving a UI change into production must require no second implementation.
nonGoals: In demo mode, no backend, relay, SQLite, worker, scheduler, Electron process, account login or production data access at runtime. Normal Electron/backend modes retain their real connections.

No separate UI copy, framework migration, visual redesign or component playground product. Refactor only dependencies needed by the three agreed areas; leave unrelated screens behind explicit host boundaries.
No real script execution, terminal, files, secrets, permission grants, chat generation, package installation or import/export.

No exhaustive backend emulation, new state-management framework, protocol redesign, login redesign or changes to permission semantics. No separate dependency installation that removes Electron from the workspace graph. Backend contract extensions, if genuinely required, must be identified before implementation and included in a reviewed revision.

sections.title: Implementation architecture
sections.body:
Target flow: **shared Vue UI → shared frontend controllers and typed access → demo / Electron / backend adapter**. Data flows back through the same view contracts. The host selects adapters at bootstrap; product components do not select transports.

Build on `PodAccess`, `remotePodAccess`, `CentralClient` and existing command/view types. Add only the missing workspace-level boundary required by Automations and Decisions. Keep interfaces small and named for real use cases; avoid a generic repository or universal command bus. Pure rendering receives props and emits typed events. Shared controllers own loading/error state, selection, refresh scheduling, invalidation and edit state; adapters own transport, response validation and operation settlement. Reuse existing cancellation, revision and unknown-outcome handling instead of weakening them.

**Demo adapter:** an explicit Vite mode injects a typed in-memory implementation. The demo store changes synthetic state only. Scenarios and toolbar live in a development-only wrapper, outside product components. No global `window.pods` replacement is the intended architecture.

**Electron adapter:** wraps the actual preload `PodsBridge`, subscribes/unsubscribes to status and forwards existing commands to the worker. Only the adapter/native host boundary may read `window.pods` for the migrated paths. It uses the same controllers and components as the demo. Both local and registered desktop entries must remain wired.

**Backend adapter:** wraps `browserWorkspaceClient` / `CentralClient` and existing `remotePodAccess`, preserves authenticated HTTP, online state, revision checks and asynchronous operations, and plugs into the same frontend. The relay's workspace page keeps its host/login responsibility. Reuse its existing imports; no copied frontend bundle or templates.

Represent genuine availability through typed capabilities, not `isDemo` branches. A local terminal or IdP action is a host service; absent capability yields the existing disabled/explanatory state. Transport mode must never grant permission. A demo capability can simulate a local effect without opening live links. Ordinary UI components must not import fixtures, Electron, Node or HTTP clients; shared data access must not fall back to a live adapter.

Before edits, inventory direct globals, transport imports, polling and native subcomponents on the three paths. Migrate these consumers together and remove superseded orchestration. Host-only UI outside scope can retain its implementation, but must not be reached accidentally in demo mode. Keep normal boot/build behavior; only explicit dev:ui conditionally imports the demo adapter and toolbar.

sections.title: Data and scenarios
sections.body:
Use invented organizations and `.invalid` identities, never copied owner mail or credentials. Seed 6–8 related Pods across two organizations: invoice review, newsletter triage, release monitoring and a morning briefing. Give them realistic summaries, tags, schedules, public variables, script snippets and several historical runs. Keep IDs, relationships, counters and statuses consistent.

| Scenario | Visible result |
| --- | --- |
| everyday | Active and paused Pods, completed runs, four pending routing questions and two groups |
| attention | A failed run with logs, a waiting IdP action and one choice that initially fails and succeeds on retry |
| empty | No Pods or decisions; existing empty-state presentation |
| loading-error | Delayed reads and an explicit recoverable read error |

A simulated run moves from running to completed after a short controlled delay and appends history. A decision changes the actual fixture state and counters across tabs. Group choices process the visible eligible cases. Changing a description, public variable or schedule remains visible after navigation.

State is memory-only in v1. Reset, scenario switching and browser reload restore the selected seed; scenario and language can be encoded in the URL. Reset cancels pending timers and clears local UI state. Hot reload remains active; fixture/module changes may reset demo state. Do not promise persistence across reloads.

sections.title: From a UI iteration to the real application
sections.body:
1. Start `pnpm --filter @openape/pods dev:ui`, select a scenario and change shared components, styles or frontend behavior.
2. Run the focused existing browser tests. If behavior or data access changes, also run the affected controller/adapter contract tests; a CSS-only edit does not require a new backend test.
3. Use the ordinary Electron/relay entry and normal build. Their bootstrap already supplies the real adapter; no copying files, changing components, toggling demo branches in screens or manual API rewiring is required. Normal installation/deployment remains the existing workflow.

Acceptance exercise: make one small visible shared-component edit and verify it in the demo, the production Electron renderer configuration and the backend-browser configuration. For a supported write, demonstrate that the same UI action dispatches through both real adapters and displays the confirmed result. Record changed files, commands and results. Real network/worker behavior is established by existing isolated backend tests, not merely by demo parity.

Backend contracts still bound what is possible: adding a new domain field or command requires its actual backend implementation and contract tests. The architecture makes that dependency explicit and local; it cannot turn new backend functionality into a mode switch. UI-only changes using existing contracts need no backend domain change.

sections.title: Test strategy and ownership
sections.body:
| Layer | What is verified | Existing location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared UI | Observable clicks, form values, disabled states, loading/error display, geometry and screenshots with real CSS | Pods `test/layout`, `test/renderer`, existing `test/workspace/*-ui.test.ts` |
| Controllers / demo state | Invalidation, consistent counters, scenario reset, timer disposal, async failure and confirmed success | Existing Pods Vitest suites; extend a fitting file or add within the suite |
| Adapter contracts | Existing request/response types, revisions, command mapping, errors, operation settlement and capabilities for demo/Electron/backend | `test/workspace/central-ui.test.ts`, `browser-workspace.test.ts`, related existing tests |
| Real boundaries | Production client/bridge handling and worker/relay effects with isolated temporary data and narrow transport doubles | Pods `test/main/worker-entry.test.ts`, workspace/storage/scheduling suites; relay `test/workspace-store.test.ts` where affected |

Keep one set of UI interaction expectations. Run the full UI scenario against the deterministic provider; parameterize a small representative smoke set across adapters using equal capabilities. Existing desktop/browser parity tests remain and gain the demo case where useful. Do not duplicate every screenshot and every interaction for all providers.

Adapter tests exercise the actual production adapter code, replacing only the external transport. For each supported command verify the expected request independently and confirm the displayed refreshed state. Cover rejected/stale revisions, unavailable capabilities, read failures and asynchronous accepted → applied / failed / unknown results. Unknown outcomes must not trigger duplicate writes. A fixture is not the expected result of its own test: use existing parsers plus explicit assertions and backend tests to avoid self-confirming mocks.

Fixtures shared with the demo provide data, not business rules or assertions. Unit tests may use controlled time; browser tests wait for visible states with bounded waits. Reset/unmount must clear subscriptions, timers and pending requests. Never weaken an assertion to match a changed mock. Preserve existing tests; remove an obsolete duplicate only when its behavior is demonstrably covered elsewhere and explain it in the PR.

Retain new tests for the durable contracts: adapter substitutability, cross-view consistency, mutation confirmation, cleanup and demo isolation. Use proportionate focused checks for purely visual edits. UI is tested in Vitest browser mode, never through new Electron E2E tests. Native/runtime changes, if any, use their existing boundary suites. No new runner, test script, test directory, mandatory CI context or default-chain change.

milestones.title: Prove transfer into Electron and the backend UI
milestones.goal: Make the few-step production handoff an explicit acceptance requirement.
steps: Apply one representative shared visual change and exercise one existing write through the production Electron and backend adapters using their isolated harnesses.
Build both affected consumers and document the ordinary startup/build path. Verify unchanged login, revision, operation and capability semantics.

The handoff is: edit shared UI → focused checks → normal host build/install or deploy. No separate integration refactor is left open.
milestones.rollback: Revert the integration and frontend change together; no deployment or signed installation is required to complete this acceptance.
milestones.proof: A temporary shared component marker appeared via Vite HMR, in the Electron and relay builds and in all three browser-mode host configurations. The marker was restored before final gates; production builds exclude demo data and toolbar.

milestones.title: Verify and document the development loop
milestones.goal: Deliver a repeatable browser workflow with inspected evidence.
steps: Extend established unit/component and Vitest browser suites for the demo contracts and critical interactions.
Capture and inspect screenshots with real CSS, verify development entry and production exclusion, publish a Test Run and document usage.
acceptance: Relevant checks pass; screenshots show all three areas at wide and narrow widths with no clipped primary controls.
Only Vite assets/HMR are requested during the demo journey; ordinary build has no demo dataset or toolbar.
The final handoff includes the start command, supported actions, scenario URLs, local server URL and verified Test Run link.
Contract and boundary evidence is separate from UI screenshots; tests prove the real adapters, not just the demo simulation.

decisions.title: One production UI
decisions.description: Use one shared frontend with injected demo, Electron and backend adapters, extending existing PodAccess and clients. Both production adapters are delivered with the refactor; no global fake bridge as the final design.

decisions.title: Memory-only state
decisions.description: Prefer deterministic reset and simple typed handlers over persistence or a generic backend simulator. No new runtime dependency is expected.

decisions.title: Browser verification
decisions.description: Share UI expectations and data builders; test contracts separately against actual adapters and existing backend handlers. Use Vitest browser mode for UI and screenshots, isolated unit/boundary tests for transport/runtime. No new Electron UI E2E or new test infrastructure.

risks.title: Fixtures drift from contracts
risks.mitigation: Type-check against PodsBridge, validate shared payloads with existing parsers and reuse builders across tests and demo.

risks.title: A click has no visible effect
risks.mitigation: Each supported command must mutate one authoritative store and refresh all derived views; unsupported actions report a limitation.

risks.title: Demo code leaks into normal operation
risks.mitigation: Explicit development mode, conditional imports, build inspection and network observation; never fall back from a missing bridge to demo data.

risks.title: Production adapters diverge from the demo
risks.mitigation: Deliver real adapters in M1 and explicit transfer acceptance in M4; check independent contracts, operation failures and capability differences. Backend additions require an explicit reviewed scope update.

entries.source: Implementation architecture
entries.text: Architektur der Umsetzung

entries.source:
Target flow: **shared Vue UI → shared frontend controllers and typed access → demo / Electron / backend adapter**. Data flows back through the same view contracts. The host selects adapters at bootstrap; product components do not select transports.

Build on `PodAccess`, `remotePodAccess`, `CentralClient` and existing command/view types. Add only the missing workspace-level boundary required by Automations and Decisions. Keep interfaces small and named for real use cases; avoid a generic repository or universal command bus. Pure rendering receives props and emits typed events. Shared controllers own loading/error state, selection, refresh scheduling, invalidation and edit state; adapters own transport, response validation and operation settlement. Reuse existing cancellation, revision and unknown-outcome handling instead of weakening them.

**Demo adapter:** an explicit Vite mode injects a typed in-memory implementation. The demo store changes synthetic state only. Scenarios and toolbar live in a development-only wrapper, outside product components. No global `window.pods` replacement is the intended architecture.

**Electron adapter:** wraps the actual preload `PodsBridge`, subscribes/unsubscribes to status and forwards existing commands to the worker. Only the adapter/native host boundary may read `window.pods` for the migrated paths. It uses the same controllers and components as the demo. Both local and registered desktop entries must remain wired.

**Backend adapter:** wraps `browserWorkspaceClient` / `CentralClient` and existing `remotePodAccess`, preserves authenticated HTTP, online state, revision checks and asynchronous operations, and plugs into the same frontend. The relay's workspace page keeps its host/login responsibility. Reuse its existing imports; no copied frontend bundle or templates.

Represent genuine availability through typed capabilities, not `isDemo` branches. A local terminal or IdP action is a host service; absent capability yields the existing disabled/explanatory state. Transport mode must never grant permission. A demo capability can simulate a local effect without opening live links. Ordinary UI components must not import fixtures, Electron, Node or HTTP clients; shared data access must not fall back to a live adapter.

Before edits, inventory direct globals, transport imports, polling and native subcomponents on the three paths. Migrate these consumers together and remove superseded orchestration. Host-only UI outside scope can retain its implementation, but must not be reached accidentally in demo mode. Keep normal boot/build behavior; only explicit dev:ui conditionally imports the demo adapter and toolbar.
entries.text:
Zielablauf: **gemeinsames Vue-UI → gemeinsame Frontend-Steuerung und typisierter Zugriff → Demo- / Electron- / Backend-Adapter**. Daten fließen über dieselben Ansichtsverträge zurück. Der Host wählt die Adapter beim Start; Produktkomponenten wählen keine Transporte aus.

Auf `PodAccess`, `remotePodAccess`, `CentralClient` und den bestehenden Befehls-/Ansichtstypen aufbauen. Nur die für Automatisierungen und Entscheidungen fehlende Workspace-Grenze ergänzen. Schnittstellen klein halten und nach tatsächlichen Anwendungsfällen benennen; kein allgemeines Repository-Framework und kein universeller Befehlsbus. Reine Darstellung erhält Props und sendet typisierte Events. Gemeinsame Steuerung verwaltet Lade-/Fehlerzustand, Auswahl, Aktualisierungsintervalle, Invalidierung und Bearbeitungszustand; Adapter verantworten Transport, Antwortvalidierung und die Abwicklung asynchroner Operationen. Bestehende Abbruch-, Revisions- und Unklarheitsbehandlung wiederverwenden und nicht abschwächen.

**Demo-Adapter:** Ein ausdrücklicher Vite-Modus setzt eine typisierte Implementierung im Speicher ein. Der Demo-Zustand verändert nur synthetische Daten. Szenarien und Werkzeugleiste liegen in einer ausschließlich für Entwicklung verwendeten Hülle außerhalb der Produktkomponenten. Ein globaler Ersatz von `window.pods` ist nicht die angestrebte Architektur.

**Electron-Adapter:** Kapselt den echten Preload-`PodsBridge`, meldet Statusabonnements an/ab und leitet bestehende Befehle an den Worker weiter. Auf den migrierten Pfaden darf nur die Adapter-/native Host-Grenze `window.pods` lesen. Dieselbe Steuerung und dieselben Komponenten wie in der Demo werden verwendet. Sowohl der lokale als auch der registrierte Desktop-Einstieg bleiben angeschlossen.

**Backend-Adapter:** Kapselt `browserWorkspaceClient` / `CentralClient` und den bestehenden `remotePodAccess`, erhält authentifiziertes HTTP, Online-Zustand, Revisionsprüfungen und asynchrone Operationen und wird in dasselbe Frontend eingesetzt. Die Workspace-Seite im Relay behält ihre Host-/Login-Aufgabe. Bestehende Imports wiederverwenden; kein kopiertes Frontend-Bundle und keine kopierten Templates.

Tatsächlich verfügbare Funktionen durch typisierte Capabilities ausdrücken, nicht durch `isDemo`-Verzweigungen. Ein lokales Terminal oder eine IdP-Aktion ist ein Host-Dienst; fehlt die Fähigkeit, erscheint der vorhandene deaktivierte/erklärende Zustand. Der Transportmodus darf niemals eine Berechtigung erteilen. Eine Demo-Fähigkeit kann eine lokale Wirkung simulieren, ohne echte Links zu öffnen. Gewöhnliche UI-Komponenten dürfen keine Fixtures, Electron, Node oder HTTP-Clients importieren; gemeinsamer Datenzugriff darf nicht auf einen echten Adapter zurückfallen.

Vor Änderungen direkte globale Zugriffe, Transport-Imports, Polling und native Unterkomponenten auf den drei Pfaden erfassen. Diese Verbraucher gemeinsam migrieren und ersetzte Steuerungslogik entfernen. Reine Host-Ansichten außerhalb des Umfangs dürfen ihre Implementierung behalten, aber nicht versehentlich im Demo-Modus erreichbar sein. Normales Start-/Build-Verhalten erhalten; nur ausdrücklich gewähltes dev:ui importiert Demo-Adapter und Werkzeugleiste bedingt.

entries.source:
Use invented organizations and `.invalid` identities, never copied owner mail or credentials. Seed 6–8 related Pods across two organizations: invoice review, newsletter triage, release monitoring and a morning briefing. Give them realistic summaries, tags, schedules, public variables, script snippets and several historical runs. Keep IDs, relationships, counters and statuses consistent.

| Scenario | Visible result |
| --- | --- |
| everyday | Active and paused Pods, completed runs, four pending routing questions and two groups |
| attention | A failed run with logs, a waiting IdP action and one choice that initially fails and succeeds on retry |
| empty | No Pods or decisions; existing empty-state presentation |
| loading-error | Delayed reads and an explicit recoverable read error |

A simulated run moves from running to completed after a short controlled delay and appends history. A decision changes the actual fixture state and counters across tabs. Group choices process the visible eligible cases. Changing a description, public variable or schedule remains visible after navigation.

State is memory-only in v1. Reset, scenario switching and browser reload restore the selected seed; scenario and language can be encoded in the URL. Reset cancels pending timers and clears local UI state. Hot reload remains active; fixture/module changes may reset demo state. Do not promise persistence across reloads.
entries.text:
Erfundene Organisationen und `.invalid`-Identitäten verwenden, keine kopierten E-Mails oder Zugangsdaten des Owners. Sechs bis acht zusammengehörige Pods in zwei Organisationen anlegen: Rechnungsprüfung, Newsletter-Sortierung, Release-Beobachtung und Morgenbriefing. Realistische Zusammenfassungen, Tags, Zeitpläne, öffentliche Variablen, Skriptausschnitte und mehrere historische Läufe ergänzen. IDs, Beziehungen, Zähler und Statuswerte bleiben konsistent.

| Szenario | Sichtbares Ergebnis |
| --- | --- |
| everyday | Aktive und pausierte Pods, abgeschlossene Läufe, vier offene Zuordnungsfragen und zwei Gruppen |
| attention | Fehlgeschlagener Lauf mit Logs, wartende IdP-Aktion und eine Entscheidung, die zunächst scheitert und beim Wiederholen gelingt |
| empty | Keine Pods oder Entscheidungen; vorhandene Darstellung leerer Zustände |
| loading-error | Verzögerte Lesezugriffe und ein ausdrücklich gemeldeter, behebbarer Lesefehler |

Ein simulierter Lauf wechselt nach einer kurzen kontrollierten Verzögerung von laufend zu abgeschlossen und ergänzt den Verlauf. Eine Entscheidung ändert den tatsächlichen Fixture-Zustand und die Zähler über die Tabs hinweg. Gruppenentscheidungen bearbeiten die sichtbaren zulässigen Fälle. Änderungen an Beschreibung, öffentlicher Variable oder Zeitplan bleiben nach Navigation sichtbar.

Version 1 hält den Zustand nur im Speicher. Zurücksetzen, Szenariowechsel und Browser-Neuladen stellen die gewählte Ausgangslage her; Szenario und Sprache können in der URL stehen. Zurücksetzen beendet ausstehende Timer und löscht lokalen UI-Zustand. Hot Reload bleibt aktiv; Änderungen an Fixtures oder Modulen können den Demo-Zustand zurücksetzen. Persistenz über Neuladen hinweg wird nicht zugesagt.

entries.source:
1. Start `pnpm --filter @openape/pods dev:ui`, select a scenario and change shared components, styles or frontend behavior.
2. Run the focused existing browser tests. If behavior or data access changes, also run the affected controller/adapter contract tests; a CSS-only edit does not require a new backend test.
3. Use the ordinary Electron/relay entry and normal build. Their bootstrap already supplies the real adapter; no copying files, changing components, toggling demo branches in screens or manual API rewiring is required. Normal installation/deployment remains the existing workflow.

Acceptance exercise: make one small visible shared-component edit and verify it in the demo, the production Electron renderer configuration and the backend-browser configuration. For a supported write, demonstrate that the same UI action dispatches through both real adapters and displays the confirmed result. Record changed files, commands and results. Real network/worker behavior is established by existing isolated backend tests, not merely by demo parity.

Backend contracts still bound what is possible: adding a new domain field or command requires its actual backend implementation and contract tests. The architecture makes that dependency explicit and local; it cannot turn new backend functionality into a mode switch. UI-only changes using existing contracts need no backend domain change.

entries.source: Test strategy and ownership
entries.text: Teststrategie und Zuständigkeit

entries.source:
| Layer | What is verified | Existing location |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared UI | Observable clicks, form values, disabled states, loading/error display, geometry and screenshots with real CSS | Pods `test/layout`, `test/renderer`, existing `test/workspace/*-ui.test.ts` |
| Controllers / demo state | Invalidation, consistent counters, scenario reset, timer disposal, async failure and confirmed success | Existing Pods Vitest suites; extend a fitting file or add within the suite |
| Adapter contracts | Existing request/response types, revisions, command mapping, errors, operation settlement and capabilities for demo/Electron/backend | `test/workspace/central-ui.test.ts`, `browser-workspace.test.ts`, related existing tests |
| Real boundaries | Production client/bridge handling and worker/relay effects with isolated temporary data and narrow transport doubles | Pods `test/main/worker-entry.test.ts`, workspace/storage/scheduling suites; relay `test/workspace-store.test.ts` where affected |

Keep one set of UI interaction expectations. Run the full UI scenario against the deterministic provider; parameterize a small representative smoke set across adapters using equal capabilities. Existing desktop/browser parity tests remain and gain the demo case where useful. Do not duplicate every screenshot and every interaction for all providers.

Adapter tests exercise the actual production adapter code, replacing only the external transport. For each supported command verify the expected request independently and confirm the displayed refreshed state. Cover rejected/stale revisions, unavailable capabilities, read failures and asynchronous accepted → applied / failed / unknown results. Unknown outcomes must not trigger duplicate writes. A fixture is not the expected result of its own test: use existing parsers plus explicit assertions and backend tests to avoid self-confirming mocks.

Fixtures shared with the demo provide data, not business rules or assertions. Unit tests may use controlled time; browser tests wait for visible states with bounded waits. Reset/unmount must clear subscriptions, timers and pending requests. Never weaken an assertion to match a changed mock. Preserve existing tests; remove an obsolete duplicate only when its behavior is demonstrably covered elsewhere and explain it in the PR.

Retain new tests for the durable contracts: adapter substitutability, cross-view consistency, mutation confirmation, cleanup and demo isolation. Use proportionate focused checks for purely visual edits. UI is tested in Vitest browser mode, never through new Electron E2E tests. Native/runtime changes, if any, use their existing boundary suites. No new runner, test script, test directory, mandatory CI context or default-chain change.
entries.text:
| Ebene | Was geprüft wird | Vorhandener Ort |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gemeinsames UI | Sichtbare Klickwirkung, Formularwerte, deaktivierte Zustände, Lade-/Fehleranzeige, Geometrie und Screenshots mit echten Styles | Pods `test/layout`, `test/renderer`, vorhandene `test/workspace/*-ui.test.ts` |
| Steuerung / Demo-Zustand | Invalidierung, konsistente Zähler, Szenario-Reset, Timer-Bereinigung, asynchrone Fehler und bestätigter Erfolg | Vorhandene Pods-Vitest-Suiten; passende Datei erweitern oder innerhalb der Suite ergänzen |
| Adapter-Verträge | Vorhandene Anfrage-/Antworttypen, Revisionen, Befehlszuordnung, Fehler, Operationsabwicklung und Capabilities für Demo/Electron/Backend | `test/workspace/central-ui.test.ts`, `browser-workspace.test.ts`, verwandte vorhandene Tests |
| Echte Grenzen | Behandlung im Produktivclient/Bridge und Worker-/Relay-Wirkungen mit isolierten temporären Daten und gezielten Transport-Doubles | Pods `test/main/worker-entry.test.ts`, Workspace-/Storage-/Scheduling-Suiten; Relay `test/workspace-store.test.ts`, soweit betroffen |

Einen gemeinsamen Satz von Erwartungen an UI-Interaktionen pflegen. Das vollständige UI-Szenario gegen den deterministischen Provider ausführen; einen kleinen repräsentativen Smoke-Umfang bei gleichen Capabilities über die Adapter parametrisieren. Vorhandene Desktop-/Browser-Paritätstests bleiben bestehen und erhalten bei Bedarf den Demo-Fall. Nicht jeden Screenshot und jede Interaktion für alle Provider duplizieren.

Adaptertests führen den tatsächlichen Produktivadapter aus und ersetzen nur den externen Transport. Für jeden unterstützten Befehl die erwartete Anfrage unabhängig prüfen und den angezeigten aktualisierten Zustand bestätigen. Abgelehnte/veraltete Revisionen, nicht verfügbare Fähigkeiten, Lesefehler und asynchrone Ergebnisse accepted → applied / failed / unknown abdecken. Unklare Ergebnisse dürfen keine doppelten Schreibzugriffe auslösen. Eine Fixture ist nicht das Soll-Ergebnis ihres eigenen Tests: vorhandene Parser, ausdrückliche Erwartungen und Backend-Tests nutzen, um selbstbestätigende Mocks zu vermeiden.

Mit der Demo geteilte Fixtures liefern Daten, keine Fachregeln oder Prüferwartungen. Unit-Tests dürfen kontrollierte Zeit nutzen; Browser-Tests warten begrenzt auf sichtbare Zustände. Reset/Unmount muss Abonnements, Timer und ausstehende Anfragen bereinigen. Erwartungen nie abschwächen, um sie an geänderte Mocks anzupassen. Bestehende Tests erhalten; ein veraltetes Duplikat nur entfernen, wenn sein Verhalten nachweislich anderswo abgedeckt ist, und dies im PR erklären.

Neue Tests für dauerhafte Verträge behalten: Austauschbarkeit der Adapter, ansichtsübergreifende Konsistenz, bestätigte Änderungen, Bereinigung und Demo-Isolation. Bei rein visuellen Änderungen verhältnismäßige gezielte Prüfungen nutzen. UI wird im Vitest-Browser-Modus geprüft, niemals durch neue Electron-E2E-Tests. Etwaige native/Laufzeitänderungen nutzen ihre vorhandenen Grenztests. Kein neuer Runner, Testbefehl, Testverzeichnis, verpflichtender CI-Kontext oder Änderung der Standard-Testkette.
